methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: AI Ready Roanoke evaluates use for new technology in Roanoke Valley - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: A regional AI readiness initiative in Roanoke Valley signals intentional peer-driven capacity building outside the NoVA corridor, potentially distributing deep capabilities through local workforce development rather than platform dependency.

signals.title: AI is already common in Virginia Beach high schools. Leaders weigh guardrails - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: AI already embedded in Virginia Beach high schools with policy debates over guardrails indicates rapid shallow adoption through educational platforms—broad distribution but focused on consumption rather than creation of AI capabilities.

signals.title: VCU partners with the Better Business Bureau to bring AI support to Central Virginia businesses - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU-BBB partnership to support Central Virginia businesses with AI training represents institutional knowledge transfer creating distributed peer networks for practical AI adoption, moving capability beyond metro consumption toward regional application depth.

signals.title: ODU, CHKD want to map hotspots of childhood asthma in Hampton Roads with AI - WHRO
signals.signal_reading: ODU-CHKD collaboration on AI-powered asthma mapping concentrates sophisticated technical capability within research institutions, creating localized excellence that may remain siloed without deliberate distribution mechanisms to community healthcare providers.

signals.title: Amazon bows to local backlash over AI data centers, scraps plans to build four new facilities in Northern Virginia — site to be repurposed for mixed-use and residential development. - Tom's Hardware
signals.signal_reading: Amazon canceling NoVA data center plans paradoxically signals infrastructure saturation blocking new AI capacity concentration while alternative regions lack the ecosystem to absorb displaced projects—deepening geographic capability asymmetry statewide.
